title: Why Visual and Vocal Interview Cues Can Affect Interviewers' Judgments and Predict Job Performance
metricDefinition: A vocal-cue composite included pitch, pitch variability, speech rate, pauses, and amplitude variability; the abstract does not expose component formulas or units.

measurements.definition: Composite representation of several vocal cues named in the abstract.
notes: Component formulas and standalone units were not available in the reviewed abstract.

reportedFindings.summary: The abstract reports an association between a vocal-cue composite and supervisory job-performance ratings.

faceFitMappings.paperMetricName: speech rate within vocal cue composite
faceFitMappings.reason: The abstract names speech rate only as part of a composite and gives no WPM definition.
Interview pauses are not defined as the sum of adjacent STT word-timestamp gaps.

faceFitMappings.paperMetricName: amplitude variability within vocal cue composite
faceFitMappings.reason: Amplitude variability is not whole-answer RMS in dBFS and capture gain is unspecified.

faceFitMappings.paperMetricName: pitch variability within vocal cue composite
faceFitMappings.reason: Pitch variability is not confirmed as maximum-minus-minimum physical F0.

thresholdAssessment.reason: The abstract reports association evidence, not a transferable behavior boundary.

limitations: Only the official abstract and registered metadata were reviewed.
The vocal cues form a composite and cannot define standalone Face-Fit metric scoring.
